title: xiaomi miui 10.2 lockscreen
body:
hello, on all xiaomi devise with miui 10.2 doesn't show notification on lockscreen

what it can be?

comments.body:
@Batista1991 on your lockscreen, with xDrip running, do you see a panel that says "Unlock to see sensitive notification" or do you simply not see any notification whatsoever concerning xDrip? If you see a panel but it simply won't reveal information, follow these steps:

1. Unlock the phone. 
1. Head over to Settings > General > Apps & notifications and select Notifications
1. If Lock screen is set to "Hide sensitive notifications only", change that to "Show all notifications". You should now be able to properly access the xDrip notification from your lockscreen.

If on the other hand you simply cannot see the xDrip notification anywhere, follow steps 1 and 2 above then:
1. Select Apps > xDrip
1. Make sure the notifications are turned on. 

Please let me know if any of this helps. Consider attaching screenshots to future issues if you think they can help.

Notifications on LockScreen are shown fine.

But MIUI 10.2 has another problem: it has not supported widgets on lockscreen. I have to unlock device every time I want to see BG graph. Using of xDrip widget on phone lockscreen would be a better solution for doing this. But it is not supported.

Another solution might be to use "Number Wall on lockscreen".. but... terrible MIUI does not support it too. It work on another devices but on MIUI calling `WallpaperManager#setBitmap(wallpaper, null, false, WallpaperManager.FLAG_LOCK);` does not have any effect without any exceptions. (with `WallpaperManager.FLAG_SYSTEM` it works fine. But that's not what I need).

So now I'm thinking to make BG graph displayed in collapsed notification. (Because it is impossible to expand notifications on lock screen).
With the new Miui 10.3.1 update, xdrip already reports the glucose level on the lock screen

Hi @karelinoleg,

Do you have found any solution to get around this on MIUI :

`WallpaperManager#setBitmap(wallpaper, null, false, WallpaperManager.FLAG_LOCK); `
